features.label: USMCA preferential rules
limitations: Cases are constructed from the General Note 11(o), 11(c), 11(e), 11(n) and 11(p) text by one author; they are not independent customs decisions or an i.i.d. sample.
The expected labels come from a separate reference oracle written from the same authority text; it does not independently validate the embedded rule data's transcription.
Cases share rule rows across inputs; source families and structural templates shared with development are counted, not hidden.
The check models simple goods; accumulation, remanufacture, automotive rules and the rayon exceptions of textile chapters are outside its scope and outside these cases.

features.label: Textile origin (19 CFR 102.21)
limitations: Cases are constructed facts for rows of 19 CFR 102.21(e); they are not CBP rulings and carry no real-world confidence interval.
The reference oracle re-encodes the used rows by hand from the eCFR text; it does not independently validate the full embedded table.
Pure tariff-shift rows and the (c)(4) most-important-process judgment are documented abstentions: expected undetermined means the check declines, not that the law has no answer.
Free-text operation names are not parsed by these cases; the facts are given as structured stages.

features.label: Tariff-watch rate changes
limitations: Every revised data set is SYNTHETIC: a constructed next revision exercising one kind of change, not a government tariff action. Tariff lines, heading numbers and baseline rates are real.
Expected figures come from arithmetic on the case's own numbers by a reference oracle that shares no code with the candidate.
Rates are compared as whole units of 0.0001 and dollars as whole cents so platform float differences cannot change a label.
Revision-text cases render synthetic heading text in the HTS PDF-extraction layout; they test the reader, not the accuracy of any real notice.

features.label: Move verification
limitations: Labels are assistant-authored variations of already-known source pairs, not independent real rulings.
Multiple variants share each source parent; case counts do not mean independent legal sources.
Known starting origin is supplied. This measures given-move verification, not full plan search or ranking.
Authority/rule label quality and date-limited retrieval affect the result. No i.i.d. population interval.

The intended source-answer isolation was incomplete: selected endpoints were excluded, but related unselected-family N357930 and N366550 remained available. N357930 was cited in three results (none shown); no causal impact is claimed. Not a source-clean independent held-out study.
Of 53 unshown positive moves, 33 had the correct target/change but insufficient shown support; 20 had a wrong change decision.
Overall agreement includes expected support withholding on incomplete facts; it is not full plan-search accuracy.
Shown precision uses the 47 shown checks, not all 220 inputs. Positive recall uses the 100 actual-change cases.
One failed model response stays in the denominator; it is not counted as a correct refusal.

One packing-control input exceeds the production 7000-character facts limit and is truncated as production would; the 93 omitted characters describe final tuning, testing and quality assurance. Its result is retained.
The v4 development prompt was worse and rejected; production v2 behavior and the 0.92 shown threshold remain unchanged.
features.public_note: Related source rulings remained available; this is not a source-clean holdout.

Reserved cases were authored by the same hand and templates as development; they were not tuned on, but shared scenario templates are disclosed (templates shared with development: 15, source families shared: 13).
No claim of 100 independent legal sources and no i.i.d. confidence interval; the cases are parameter variations of a small set of rules and rulings.

Only rows whose whole product-specific rule is CC, CTH or CTSH, in machinery, instruments and metal articles, were used; failing materials always exceed any tolerance or de minimis. Two of the 8 declined decided cases are among them. There is no production arm on the reserved Japan cases, so the study cannot say whether the Japan candidate helped; it is not wired on this evidence.

features.label: BOM image extraction
limitations: Synthetic renderings of ruling-derived illustrative fixtures, not real photos, handwriting or independent customs cases. The original primary rulings were not newly reread for this image study.
Related documents share source components and layouts. Source families are disjoint across development and reserved test; eight rendering styles are shared, four are test-only.
Names use exact case/whitespace-normalized matching, not a model judge. Country aliases use a fixed map. Semantically equivalent paraphrases can therefore fail.

Whole-document agreement requires all expected confirmed parts and countries, no extra confirmed parts, and a warning plus no invented country for every missing-origin part. The production API withholds missing-country rows from confirmed components.
The language variation changes column headers only; the component names remain as in the English source fixtures.

The missing-origin footer explicitly says the supplier address is not a statement of part origin. Withholding 11/11 is on a self-labelled distractor in one layout, not an unlabelled-address challenge.
The bundled font can leave a visible glyph gap before the closing parenthesis. The strict scorer still treats the model's inserted space as a mismatch, not a legal or wrong-origin error.

All three reserved mismatches are an extra space before a closing parenthesis in the PCBA name; the three extracted rows are unmatched names, not independently established invented parts. Strict first scores remain unchanged.
features.public_note: 52/132 sheets have only 1–2 parts; 21/24 sheets with 12+ parts matched.
